bugs.origin: A (implementation) with a wrong B pre-check premise (K32)
steps: Production build of the working tree (remix-serve) and dev server :5173, 1440x900 and 1280x720, fresh context.
Open /studio-lab, wait until all 9 sources are ready, wait 2.5 s, HeapProfiler.collectGarbage x2, list every live AudioBuffer by duration (probe in c-round-382/lib.mjs).
Wait 10 s more, GC x2, list again.
bugs.expected: Task 2/EVICT-BROWSER (a): no live buffer of 150.37 s or 101.35 s at ready; live PCM about 31.9 MiB, 7 buffers, 0 decode.
bugs.actual: The 150.37 s hero MP3 buffer (55.07 MiB) stays live at ready and after 10 s: live list [2,5,16,16,16,16,16,150.37] s, 8 buffers, 86.93 MiB (ctor 31.86 + decode 55.07), identical in 4/4 runs, both viewports, dev and prod. The perf spec agrees: res.mem.pcm-live-mib-ready 86.9, count 8, decode 55.1 (3 samples each). The perf-plan target (<= 60 MB at ready) is missed. Only the 101.35 s file is released. Measured pattern (not a confirmed holder): exactly one decoded MP3 buffer, the most recently decoded or previewed one, stays alive and is released only when the next MP3 is decoded (preview middle-east drops hero; preview hero drops middle-east; after-export delta -18 = -55 hero +37 middle-east). It is app-side: the probe and the perf registry treat both MP3s identically, so an asymmetric result cannot come from the instrument. The common path is collection.loadSource -> fetchAndDecodeSource (source-fetch.ts) -> decodeAudioData. The ensureDecoded path used by preview does not call requestSourcePeaks, so the peaks job cannot be the only holder, and at ready nothing was played, so the preview player cannot be either. I read studio-lab-demo.ts l.100-140 and source-fetch.ts l.1-35 and found no module-level last-result memo; the holder is not found, B/A should use a heap snapshot (retainers of the live 150.37 s / 101.35 s AudioBuffer). Same mechanism as C-R382-02: one fix is expected to close both; B may merge.
